text:
maya: Hey team — kicking off a PRD intake for a Rollout Evaluation Harness. Want to capture problem, goals, acceptance, and edge cases. Posting a first-draft intake below. Please react and add short replies rather than long threads so we can iterate.
maya: Problem statement: we currently rely on ad-hoc eval runs and manual smoke checks before model rollouts. This leads to slow roll cycles, missed regressions, and inconsistent quality for customer-facing deployments.
maya: Goal: build a standardized, automated "rollout eval harness" that runs a short, reproducible suite of checks (quality, latency, resource usage, stability) as a gating step for canary and GA rollouts.
maya: Non-goals: this is NOT a full offline evaluation platform. Not solving long-form human labeling workflows or cross-model benchmarking in v1.
maya: Success metrics (initial):
- % of rollouts with automated gate run >= 90% within 2 months
- Reduce rollback rate due to quality regressions by 30% in first quarter after launch
- Mean time to detect regressions during rollout < 30 minutes (from canary start)
maya: Core requirements (v1):
1) Pluggable test suites: small sets (50-200) of labeled prompts per integration + metric definitions (accuracy/LL, hallucination rate, embedding drift, latency percentiles).
2) Fast execution target: full harness completes within 15 minutes for canary size (5% traffic).
3) Deterministic configuration: manifests stored with rollout config and commit id.
4) Thresholds + policy: configurable pass/fail thresholds and automatic pause/rollback triggers for canary/AB.
5) Visibility: results surfaced in Console and rollout logs + alert hooks.
maya: Acceptance criteria (suggested):
```
- Harness can be triggered automatically on canary start for any model variant in Dedicated/Hosted.
- Results include at least: token-level latency p50/p95, response-quality score (qa metric), a binary hallucination signal, and system resource snapshot.
- Console shows pass/fail with diff vs baseline and link to raw logs.
- Policy engine pauses rollout if any critical metric crosses threshold for >2 minutes.
- End-to-end run completes for common 7B/13B configs within 15 minutes on standard dedicated pool.
```
maya: Edge cases we should call out:
- Flaky tests due to non-deterministic model outputs -> need randomized seed control and multiple-run averaging.
- Small-sample noise for low-traffic canaries -> consider minimum sample sizes or sequential testing.
- Network blips causing latency spikes unrelated to model -> distinguish infra vs model regressions.
- Customer-specific data constraints (PII) -> harness must support anonymized prompt sets.
maya: Implementation notes / rough plan:
- Phase 0 (2w): define manifest format, minimal CLI trigger, and an example test suite for summarization + classification.
- Phase 1 (4w): integrate with rollout controller to auto-trigger, store results, and add Console view.
- Phase 2 (4w): policy engine + alerts + support for embedding drift checks.

maya: Questions for reviewers:
- sam: Is 15 minutes achievable for typical canary using our batching/caching?
- ananya: What quality metrics should be canonical for v1? Accuracy + hallucination?
- liam: UI constraints — do we have space to surface diffs without a separate page?
- tj: Any design constraints for showing pass/fail with minimal noise?

sam: 15m is tight but doable if we run small suites and leverage cached KV for prompt prefixes. Need an infra SLA for pre-warming canary nodes.

ananya: For v1 I'd pick: QA F1 (where applicable), exact-match for classification, hallucination-rate (model asserts unsupported facts), and embedding cosine drop for retrieval use cases. Keep composite score simple.

liam: Console: we can add a compact card on rollout detail page with pass/fail, delta to baseline, and a link "Open harness report". Avoid new top-level nav.
tj: Design: prioritize signal over noise. Show an overall status (green/yellow/red), top 3 failing checks, and an expandable raw logs view. Use tooltips for thresholds.

maya: +1 on those suggestions. For the manifest schema, thinking of a small YAML like:
```
name: summarization-smoke-v1
prompts: s3://redwood-evals/summ-smoke/2026-01-20.jsonl
metrics:
  - name: rouge-l
    threshold: 0.28
  - name: hallucination_rate
    threshold: 0.05
traffic_sample: 0.05
policy:
  on_fail: pause
  severity: critical
```

ananya: Add sampling_seed and replicate_runs fields so we can average across runs.

sam: Need to call out resource snapshotting: memory, GPU util, and model kv cache hit rate. That helps debug perf regressions.

maya: Good point. Will add. Also adding: "baseline" pointer to prior validated commit id for diffing.

ops-bot: Reminder: schedule an on-call review for rollout policy changes. Use #eng-oncall for signoff.

liam: One more ask: exportable JSON for run results so customers can pull via API for audit logs.

maya: Agree — results API required.

maya: Next steps: I'll update this intake with manifest schema + minimal run CLI in the next 24h. Please add short reactions or reply here with any red flags. If no major objections, I'll move to draft PRD and tag @sam @ananya for acceptance criteria sign-off.
